spec_deviations.deviation: 'Payload keys verbatim' vs 'optimizer-stripped': the two pattern requirements conflict on one key.
spec_deviations.resolution: Lock payload = the trainer checkpoint key set MINUS optim_state_dict (stripped by ops section 3 item 4 / G5) PLUS two additive marks checkpoint_flavor='lock' and lock_binding; recurrent_hidden lives inside the single rank runtime only (not duplicated top-level as in train_fact_surrogate) so one shape serves both lineages; loader rejects trainer-flavored and optimizer-carrying payloads. The existing trainer loader contract is untouched (nothing in train_distributed.py / train_fact_surrogate.py was modified).
spec_deviations.reason: Optimizer-stripping is the defining clause of the lock variant (ops section 3 item 4); the flavor mark keeps lock vs state-complete distinguishable under the shared format_version 2.

spec_deviations.deviation: torch.save to a PATH embeds the destination filename as the zip archive root (verified: same content saved to two filenames yields different bytes), which would make lock bytes depend on path/pid and violate same-inputs-byte-identical-outputs.
spec_deviations.resolution: Canonical serialization via io.BytesIO then atomic byte write; verified byte-identical across processes and loadable under any filename.
spec_deviations.reason: Byte-determinism is a hard build rule and underpins the G4 sha256 lock; the buffer form is the only canonical torch serialization.

spec_deviations.deviation: numpy 2.4.4 np.random.get_state() returns a live-aliased keys array (a later seed()/set_state() mutates the stored tuple), so an uncopied capture is not a frozen snapshot.
spec_deviations.resolution: _numpy_rng_snapshot() copies the keys array at capture.
spec_deviations.reason: A lock must freeze its RNG runtime, not alias it.

spec_deviations.deviation: Contracts section 2.5 says the lock variant is 'emitted alongside the state-complete format'; wiring save_lock_checkpoint into trainer loops was NOT done.
spec_deviations.resolution: Deferred to the D0 training-window step as the task default allows: the emission clause describes trainer behavior at authorized training time; pre-D0 wiring would be dead code untestable without a training run, and ecomd/training/train_distributed.py is explicitly out of modification scope. The build register item itself is 'lock-checkpoint variant + binding sidecar', both delivered.
spec_deviations.reason: Conservative scope: the spec does not demand trainer integration now (no [D0 BUILD] sub-item says so); nothing silently omitted.

spec_deviations.deviation: Ambiguity in 'corpus/prestate hash' and 'corpus-manifest binding' field vocabulary.
spec_deviations.resolution: Adopted E-1 projector vocabulary verbatim (corpus_hash / prestate_hash mandatory 64-hex; tape_hash / manifest_hash optional None-able), format-validated; schema_version defaults to 'lab-asset-v3' (G3 anchor vocabulary).
spec_deviations.reason: Single frozen hash grammar across build items; narrower than inventing new fields.

spec_deviations.deviation: Spec does not state whether n_draws is validated or merely recorded.
spec_deviations.resolution: Hard-validated n_draws == K_INFERENCE_DRAWS (16, C16 item 11; G8/G10 check n_draws == 16) at binding construction and in verification; save also requires at least one named-substream generator from SUBSTREAM_NAMES.
spec_deviations.reason: Conservative/narrower reading: a lock recording anything else is malformed by construction.

interface_notes: Sidecar convention lock_sidecar_path = '<checkpoint>.lock.json'; sidecar content is path-free, so the (checkpoint, sidecar) pair stays verifiable after relocation together; the D0 lock manifest (G4, analyzer checkpoint_lock_sha256) is the external anchor against fully self-consistent forgeries, which no self-contained instrument can detect.

verify_lock(deep=False) is the verifiable-without-loading-weights surface (contracts section 2.5(ii) G4/G10 self-containedness): re-hashes checkpoint file bytes vs checkpoint_sha256 and recomputes the binding chain sha256(canonical JSON of binding: model hash + config hash + corpus binding + seed/kernel/n_draws/iter). deep=True additionally torch.loads and proves weights/config/runtime/binding inside the file match the sidecar (catches a weights rewrite with a repaired file hash).

load_lock_checkpoint defaults verify=True and raises ValueError listing all failures, so a surgery cell (C11) or reflexive cell (C12) cannot start from an unverified lock; it restores named-substream generators that continue their exact pre-lock streams and returns (does not auto-apply) the torch/numpy/python global states for callers that must restore the ambient runtime.

save_lock_checkpoint hashes the checkpoint file AFTER os.replace, so the sidecar always matches on-disk bytes; writes are atomic (pid-suffixed temp + os.replace + fsync) with crash-leftover tolerance (own temps cleaned on failure; foreign stale temps inert); a sidecar-write failure after a checkpoint replace is loudly detected by verification (checkpoint_sha256 mismatch), never silently accepted.
The module has no stochastic consumer (global-RNG states are captured, never consumed); it persists nothing itself - callers choose destinations. Tests persist only under tmp_path.
model_state_sha256 is dtype/shape/name-length-prefixed raw-bytes hashing with a uint8-view fallback for numpy-hostile dtypes (bfloat16), so it works for both lineages' state dicts.
